questions.text: In the reading, Kamila adds "if" to her plans because:
opts: Plans with conditions feel less stressful when things change
She doesn't like making promises at all
questions.correct: Plans with conditions feel less stressful when things change
questions.hint: Paragraph 3: "If you make plans with conditions, you don't feel bad when things change."

questions.text: Amir writes all his plans in a notebook every Sunday.
questions.hint: Amir acts immediately — Kamila writes in a notebook, not Amir.

questions.text: Dr. Akhmetov says language and life are:
opts: The same — both use conditionals every day
questions.correct: The same — both use conditionals every day
questions.hint: Paragraph 6: "Language and life are the same."

questions.text: Kamila and Amir agree to meet:
questions.hint: Dialogue: "If the library is open, we will study together."

questions.text: Kamila says that learning conditionals makes English your "thinking ___".
questions.hint: Dr. Akhmetov: "English becomes your thinking tool."

questions.text: Zhibek's plan for summer depends on:
questions.hint: Listening: Zhibek said "If it is hot this summer, I will travel to the mountains."

questions.text: Gulnaz uses which type of conditional?
questions.hint: Gulnaz used zero conditional (press button → starts) and also zero truth statements.

questions.text: Rustam's team is certain to win the tournament.
questions.hint: Rustam said "if" his team wins — it is a condition, not a certainty.

questions.text: Zhibek says if she gets a scholarship, she will:
questions.hint: Listening: Zhibek said "If I get a scholarship, I will study abroad."

questions.text: Rustam says "If we practise every day, we ___ next month."
questions.hint: First conditional — Rustam's statement about the team.

questions.text: Zero conditional uses:
questions.hint: Zero conditional — both clauses in present simple. No "will".

questions.text: First conditional result clause uses:
questions.hint: First conditional: If + present simple, WILL + infinitive.

questions.text: If you ___ (not water) the plants, they will die.
questions.hint: Negative if-clause: don't + verb.

questions.text: "If I will study, I will pass" is correct first conditional.
questions.hint: Never use "will" in the if-clause! Correct: "If I study, I will pass."

questions.text: If you mix red and yellow, you ___ orange.
questions.hint: This is a scientific fact — zero conditional, present simple.

questions.text: She ___ (be) happy if you visit her.
questions.hint: First conditional: will + infinitive in the result clause.

questions.text: "When" can replace "if" in the zero conditional when:
opts: The event is always true or always happens
The sentence is about the future
questions.correct: The event is always true or always happens
questions.hint: "When" is used for regular, habitual, or always-true situations.

questions.text: Which is a first conditional?
opts: If plants die, they need water.
If Amir wins, he will celebrate.
If ice gets cold, it stays solid.
When she is tired, she rests.
questions.correct: If Amir wins, he will celebrate.
questions.hint: If + present simple, will + infinitive = first conditional.

questions.text: If we don't hurry, we ___ (miss) the bus.
questions.hint: First conditional: will + miss.

questions.text: Zero conditional is used for real, possible future situations.
questions.hint: Zero conditional is for facts/truths. FIRST conditional is for future possibilities.

questions.text: "Condition" means:
opts: A requirement that must be met for something to happen
questions.correct: A requirement that must be met for something to happen
questions.hint: A condition = something that must be true for the result to occur.

questions.text: "Immediately" means:
questions.hint: "Immediately" = at once, right now.

questions.text: A "promise" and a "condition" are the same thing.
questions.hint: A promise = commitment; a condition = requirement. Different meanings.

questions.text: She explained the ___ clearly: no phones during the exam.
questions.hint: A "rule" = an instruction or regulation you must follow.

questions.text: "General truth" refers to:
opts: A story that is slightly true
A fact that is always correct, not just sometimes
questions.correct: A fact that is always correct, not just sometimes
questions.hint: "General truth" = something universally true, like "water boils at 100°C".

questions.text: "Possibility" is closest in meaning to:
questions.hint: "Possibility" = the chance that something might happen.

questions.text: "If" always begins the sentence in a conditional.
questions.hint: The if-clause can come second: "I will help you if I finish early."

questions.text: "Expand" means:
questions.hint: "Expand" = to become bigger or broader.

questions.text: A "forecast" is:
questions.hint: "Forecast" = a prediction, especially about weather.

questions.text: If you work hard, you will ___ your goal.
questions.hint: "Achieve" = to succeed in reaching a goal through effort.
